Caleb Martin is an American professional basketball player.
Caleb Martin plays for the Philadelphia 76ers of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
Caleb Martin played college basketball for the NC State Wolfpack and the Nevada Wolf Pack.
Caleb Martin was named the Mountain West Conference Player of the Year for the 2017–18 season by the league's coaches.
Caleb Martin is the twin brother of Cody Martin.
Caleb Martin began his NBA career in the 2019–20 season.
Caleb Martin played two seasons with the Charlotte Hornets before signing with the Miami Heat.
Caleb Martin helped the Miami Heat reach the NBA Finals in 2023.
Caleb Martin is a 6 ft 5 in (1.96 m) small forward from Mocksville, North Carolina.
Caleb Martin played basketball for prep powerhouse Oak Hill Academy with twin brother Cody Martin.
Caleb and his brother played three seasons at Davie County High School in Mocksville before playing at Oak Hill.
Caleb Martin played football his freshman year of high school.
Caleb and his brother committed to North Carolina State University to play for coach Mark Gottfried.
As a sophomore, Caleb Martin averaged 11.5 points and 4.7 rebounds per game.
Following the season, the Martin twins chose to transfer to Nevada to play for coach Eric Musselman.
Caleb Martin sat out the 2016–17 season due to NCAA transfer rules.
In his debut season at Nevada, Caleb Martin averaged 18.9 points per game.
Caleb Martin was named Mountain West Conference Player of the Year from the league's coaches in his debut season.
Caleb Martin shared Player of the Year honors with Boise State's Chandler Hutchison.
Caleb Martin led the Wolf Pack to a regular season conference championship and a Top 25 ranking.
Caleb and his brother led the team to the 2018 NCAA tournament, where they advanced to the Sweet 16 after coming back from double-digits in wins over Texas and Cincinnati.
After finishing out his junior season, Caleb Martin and his brother both tested out the 2018 NBA draft and were in the NBA Draft Combine that year.
Both Caleb and Cody ultimately decided to return for their senior seasons at Nevada.
Coming into his senior season, Caleb Martin was named Preseason Mountain West Player of the Year.
Caleb Martin averaged 19.2 points per game, 5.1 rebounds, and 2.8 assists during his senior season.
Caleb Martin led Nevada to a 29–5 (15–3 MW) record during his senior season.
Caleb Martin's college career ended with a loss in the First Round of the NCAA tournament to Florida 61–70.
Caleb Martin was named to First-Team All Mountain West following the season along with fellow teammate Jordan Caroline.
Caleb Martin was undrafted in the 2019 NBA draft.
On July 31, 2019, Caleb Martin signed with the Charlotte Hornets on a two-way contract.
Cody Martin was selected in the second round of the 2019 NBA draft.
On October 19, 2019, the Hornets converted Caleb Martin's contract into a two-way contract.
Later the same day, Caleb Martin agreed to a multi-year deal with the Hornets and was converted to a standard deal.
On October 25, 2019, Caleb Martin made his NBA debut, coming off the bench in a 99–121 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves with four points, two rebounds, three assists, two blocks, and a steal.
On November 27, 2019, Caleb Martin received his first assignment to the Hornets NBA G League affiliate, the Greensboro Swarm.
On March 9, 2020, Caleb Martin scored a season-high 23 points, alongside four assists, three steals, and two blocks, in a 138–143 double overtime loss to the Atlanta Hawks.
On April 13, 2021, Caleb Martin scored a season-high 17 points, alongside ten rebounds, and five assists, in a 93–101 loss to the Los Angeles Lakers.
On May 4, 2021, Caleb Martin again scored 17 points, alongside five rebounds, two assists, and two steals, in a 102–99 win over the Detroit Pistons.
On August 7, 2021, Caleb Martin was waived by the Hornets.
On September 14, 2021, Caleb Martin signed with the Miami Heat on a two-way contract, splitting time with the Sioux Falls Skyforce.
He made his Heat debut on October 21, recording five points and two steals in a 137–95 win over the Milwaukee Bucks.
On December 8, 2021, Caleb Martin scored a career-high 28 points, alongside eight rebounds, three assists, and two steals, in a 113–104 win over the Bucks.
On February 15, 2022, the Heat converted Caleb Martin's contract to a standard deal.
During the playoffs, the Heat faced the Atlanta Hawks during their first round series. Caleb Martin made his playoff debut on April 17, scoring two points in a 115–91 Game 1 win.
The Heat reached the Eastern Conference Finals but were eliminated in seven games by the Boston Celtics.
On July 6, 2022, Caleb Martin re-signed with the Heat on a 3-year, $20 million deal.
On October 22, 2022, during a 112–109 win over the Toronto Raptors, Caleb Martin was ejected after an altercation with Raptors center Christian Koloko.
The next day, the NBA suspended Caleb Martin for one game without pay due to the altercation.

During the first round of the 2023 NBA playoffs, Caleb Martin played a key role in the eight-seed Heat upsetting the top-seeded Milwaukee Bucks, averaging 11.2 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 2 assists per game.
On May 19, 2023, Caleb Martin scored 25 points during a 111–105 Game 2 Eastern Conference Finals win against the Boston Celtics.
In Game 7 of the series, Caleb Martin scored 26 points and grabbed 10 rebounds in a 103–84 win, helping the Heat advance to their second NBA Finals appearance in four years.

Caleb Martin came one vote short of besting teammate Jimmy Butler for Eastern Conference Finals MVP while averaging 19.3 points and 6.4 rebounds per game, shooting 60.2% from the field and 48.9% from three.
Caleb Martin struggled in the NBA Finals, averaging only 7.4 points on 37.5% shooting.
The Heat lost the Finals in 5 games to the Denver Nuggets.
On July 6, 2024, Caleb Martin signed with the Philadelphia 76ers on a multi-year contract.
